title: [narrowed from the-newly-failing-gate-attributes-load-sensitive-timeouts-to-the-draft] The newly-failing-test gate block
description:
[narrowed from the-newly-failing-gate-attributes-load-sensitive-timeouts-to-the-draft] The newly-failing-test gate blocks correct changes by attributing load-sensitive TIMEOUTS to the draft under review. Its second-run reproduction check cannot tell a timeout apart from a regression, because a slow test stays slow on the retry.

OBSERVED 2026-09-10 on compose route-edit-e2e2e592, a two-line dead-code removal in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/learning-signal-health-observer.ts that deleted two unused const declarations and nothing else. Both edits applied (apply_failed false), typecheck passed (TC_EXIT=0), shape-dispatch passed (SD_EXIT=0). The verdict was UNFAVORABLE and the semantic gate never even ran (addresses null, reason null). The blocking line was:

    NEW test failures introduced by this draft, REPRODUCED on a second run (1):
    (fail) vessel_mitosis_cutover > freshness gate: refuses cutover when staged_base_sha is missing

THE ATTRIBUTION IS FALSE, AND THE CONTROL IS CHEAP. The edited file is src/resolvers/learning-signal-health-observer.ts; the failing test exercises test/resolvers/vessel-mitosis-cutover.test.ts. There is no import path between them, and the deleted constants were read by nothing. Running that test file on a CLEAN tree with no draft applied reproduces the failure:

    (fail) vessel_mitosis_cutover > freshness gate: refuses cutover when staged_base_sha is missing [5001.02ms]
    (fail) vessel_mitosis_cutover > git-aware cutover: applies staged files, commits, mirrors to /vessels [5001.60ms]
    21 pass, 2 fail

THE MECHANISM IS A TIMEOUT, NOT AN ASSERTION. Both durations are 5001ms against a 5000ms limit. These tests spawn git and filesystem work and are load-sensitive: in a quiet baseline run they pass, and during a compose - which is running typechecks and model calls concurrently, at a host load average around 8 - they exceed the limit. That is why the reproduction check confirms rather than filters them: the second run happens under the same load as the first, so a slow test is slow twice. "Reproduced" is being read as "caused by the draft" when it only establishes "not a one-off flake".

WHY THIS MATTERS. The gate is the last thing standing between a correct change and a landing, and it is rejecting on a signal unrelated to the change. The composer's own hard anchor-failure rate has been measured at 20-23% since 2026-09-08 against a 10-12% baseline; if a share of the remaining verdict losses are false blocks of this kind, effort spent on the drafter and the judge is aimed at the wrong component. It also interacts badly with the fact that this vessel currently carries 28 pre-existing test failures out of 2,235: a noisy baseline makes every comparison less reliable.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT. Distinguish a timeout from an assertion failure before attributing it: a test that fails by exceeding its time limit is not evidence about a diff unless the diff plausibly touches its execution path. At minimum, exclude timeout-class failures from newly-failing attribution and report them separately as an environment signal; better, re-run a suspected new failure in isolation, unloaded, before blocking on it, since an isolated re-run is exactly what distinguishes the two. Raising the limit on these specific tests would also work but treats one instance rather than the class.

NOTE THE COMPLEMENTARY DEFECT ALREADY KNOWN. computeNewlyFailing returns NO new failures when the baseline is null or empty, so it fails open in one direction and, as shown here, false-blocks in the other. Both stem from treating a noisy comparison as authoritative.

VERIFY BEHAVIOURALLY. Dispatch a provably inert change - for example deleting an unused local - and confirm it is not blocked by a failing test in a file with no import relationship to the edited module. Reading the source cannot establish this; it needs the compose report.

SECOND INSTANCE, 2026-09-10 ~11:40, AND THIS ONE BLOCKED A DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY CHANGE.

Compose route-edit-e40558ea, one op against repos/ias-executor-ts/src/adapters/activity-api-provider.ts. The change adds a single console.warn to a branch that already returns null, so it cannot alter control flow or any value. The compose report records:

    verdict: UNFAVORABLE
    apply_failed: false          <- the edit applied cleanly
    op_count: 1                  <- single operation
    rolled_back: true
    semantic_gate.addresses: null <- the judge NEVER RAN
    summary: "deterministic edit synthesized from the goal's verbatim old→new replacement"

Note the summary: the composer recognised a verbatim old→new pair and synthesized the edit DETERMINISTICALLY, with no model drafting involved. So this is the cleanest possible case — a one-line, machine-synthesized, provably inert diagnostic — and it was still refused, before any semantic judgement, by the gate that precedes it.

WHY THIS INSTANCE MATTERS MORE THAN THE FIRST. The change being blocked is the one that makes this class of failure diagnosable at all: it adds the missing log line to ActivityApiTemplateProvider.getTemplate, whose silent nulls are why a template that activity-api serves with HTTP 200 is reported by goal-host as absent, and why that investigation took seven hypotheses. So the test gate is currently blocking the instrumentation needed to diagnose a separate defect - a false block with a compounding cost, not merely a wasted draft.

TWO ATTEMPTS, SAME OUTCOME. Dispatched twice, roughly forty minutes apart, both reaching fc-plan and neither producing a semantic verdict. That rules out a one-off: whatever the gate is comparing against is failing this diff consistently, and consistently for reasons unrelated to the diff, which is exactly the failure mode this gap describes.

THE SECOND INSTANCE IS NOT A TIMEOUT — IT IS A CORRUPTED TEST TREE, AND THAT IS A DIFFERENT AND WORSE MECHANISM.

Reading the verify block of route-edit-e40558ea rather than assuming it matched the first instance:

    compose environment:   134 pass, 32 fail, 30 ERRORS, 166 tests across 46 files
    clean tree, same repo:  372 pass, 23 fail,  0 errors, 395 tests across 50 files

The compose ran FEWER FILES (46 vs 50) and produced 30 ERRORS. Errors at that count are module-load failures, not assertion failures and not timeouts. A one-line console.warn added to a branch that already returns null cannot remove four test files from a run or prevent modules from loading.

The gate's own message names the symptom precisely — "PASSING TESTS DISAPPEARED: 353 -> 134 (a draft must not delete coverage or break module load to go green)" — and that rule is CORRECT. A draft really must not delete coverage. The defect is the attribution: the coverage vanished for a reason the draft did not cause, and the gate has no way to tell the difference.

THE LIKELY CAUSE TIES THIS TO THE CONCURRENT-COMPOSE CLASS. Composes share working trees; this substrate has already recorded both directions of that contention — "SKIPPING ROLLBACK ... file content has changed (likely by another concurrent compose)" on the refusal side, and a cutover committing another gap's staged edit under its own attribution on the landing side. A third consequence follows directly: another compose's IN-FLIGHT, HALF-APPLIED edit sitting in the shared tree while this draft's suite runs will break module load for whatever files import it, and every one of those failures is then attributed to the draft under test.

That converts an intermittent nuisance into a systematic one. It is not load-sensitive and not random: it fires whenever two composes overlap on one vessel, which on a continuously-running lane is most of the time. It also explains why two attempts forty minutes apart failed identically — not a flake reproducing, but a shared tree that was dirty on both occasions.

NOTE ALSO: the clean tree carries 23 pre-existing failures of its own. So the baseline this gate differences against is noisy even before contention, which is the condition the original entry above describes.

VERIFY BEHAVIOURALLY, REVISED. Run the same provably-inert one-line diff twice: once while no other compose touches that vessel, and once during a concurrent compose on it. If the first passes and the second reports vanished coverage, the attribution defect is contention, not flake, and the fix is isolation of the test tree rather than better flake filtering.

WHY PREVIOUS ATTEMPTS ON THIS GAP FAILED (most recent last):
- wrong_location: adversarial refuters agreed 2/2 (conf 0.95, 0.90): The timeout detection filter at lines 2190-2191 is fundamentally broken: `f.includes('[5001')` only catches timeouts of exactly 5001.x ms (missing 50
- compose_execution_failure: {"error":"no_unique_anchor: refused fs_edit — planned anchor is non-unique and re-derivation found no unique substring (would mislocalize to first occurrence)"}
- semantic_reject: adversarial refuters agreed 2/2 (conf 0.90, 0.90): The patch only superficially addresses the gap by filtering out timeouts, but still relies on the underlying mechanism that fails to correctly attrib

Do not repeat these failures. Address the specific cause named above.
